authors: Erik Brynjolfsson and Bharat Chandar and Ruyu Chen
title: Canaries in the Coal Mine? Six Facts about the Recent Employment Effects of Artificial Intelligence
verification: Primary abstract and institutional release verified
verified_finding: Age 22–25 employment shortfall of 19% relative to keeping pace with less-exposed peers; hiring rather than separations is the principal margin.
caveat: Descriptive; education attenuates patterns; some divergence predates GenAI; survey benchmarks differ.

authors: Seyed Mahdi Hosseini Maasoum and Guy Lichtinger
title: Generative AI as Seniority-Biased Technological Change: Evidence from U.S. Résumé and Job Posting Data
verification: Primary seminar abstract verified; revised full text inaccessible
data: US resumes and postings; original seminar 62 million workers / 285,000 firms
verified_finding: Primary seminar supports junior decline associated with slower hiring.
caveat: User-reported revised 8–10% estimate and revised 65 million / 280,000 sample not independently checked in full paper; do not combine sample vintages.
version: 2025 primary seminar; SSRN lists June 2026 revision

authors: Cody Orr and Lee C. Tucker and Lawrence Warren
title: Graduating into Disruption: Labor Market Outcomes for AI-Exposed College Majors
verified_finding: Top exposure decile initial employment probability −5 percentage points and full-quarter initial earnings −13%.
caveat: Major-level entry outcome, not all youth or occupational wage effect; about half earnings decline reflects sectoral movement.

title: You’re (not) Hired: Artificial Intelligence and Early Career Hiring in the Quarterly Workforce Indicators
verified_finding: Most-exposed quintile adjusted employment fell 12% over ten quarters; lower hires principal driver; hiring rate largely recovered by early 2025.
caveat: Hiring counts and rates differ; supplied 9% hiring figure not independently checked; pretrend concern retained for discussion, not represented as newly replicated.

title: Generative AI and Labor Market Outcomes: Evidence from the United Kingdom
verification: Bibliography verified in Chandar–Klein Teeselink; full text inaccessible
data: UK LinkedIn/Revelio and postings, user-supplied description
verified_finding: No exact coefficient independently verified in this audit.
caveat: User-supplied −4.5% / −5.8% retained only as unverified claims, excluded from verified evidence synthesis.

title: Young workers’ employment drops in occupations with high AI exposure
data: US CPS; young 20–24 and prime-age 25–55; through September 2025
verified_finding: Young exposed employment weakness associated chiefly with reduced non-participation-to-employment entry; limited aggregate unemployment implication.
caveat: Research note, not causal paper; age band differs from our 22–25; original date January 6, not March repost date.

authors: Bharat Chandar and Bouke Klein Teeselink
title: How Does AI Change Labor Demand? Evidence from 41 Countries
data: 1.25 billion postings; 154 million employment records; multinational affiliates; through March 2026
design: Instrumented event study; parent-headquarters peer adoption instrument
verified_finding: Junior employment share −1.9 pp; senior employment +6.7%; junior headcount −2.5%, insignificant.
caveat: Junior share decline does not imply junior job destruction; IV exclusion restriction and digitally attached multinational selection matter.

title: Still Waters, Rapid Currents: Early Labor Market Transformation under Generative AI
verification: Author institutional summary verified; revised NBER full text inaccessible
data: Danish adoption surveys linked to administrative records through December 2024
design: Adoption DiD at worker and workplace levels
verified_finding: Author October 2026 account reports earnings and hours nulls excluding average effects above 2%; no differential workplace headcount or hiring-composition changes.
caveat: Do not confuse May 2025 BFI version, titled Large Language Models, Small Labor Market Effects, which reports a 1% bound, with revised 2% statement. US transportability and post-2024 horizon limited.

authors: Morgan R. Frank and Alireza Javadian Sabet and Lisa Simon and Sarah H. Bana and Renzhe Yu
title: AI-exposed jobs deteriorated before ChatGPT
data: US unemployment insurance; LinkedIn profiles; university syllabi
verified_finding: Exposed occupational unemployment risk rose in early 2022; entry gaps predate ChatGPT; exposed curricula also associated with favourable first-job outcomes.
caveat: Challenges release-date attribution; does not establish zero causal AI effects under every adoption definition.

authors: Peter John Lambert and Yannick Schindler
title: The Broken Ladder: AI, Remote Work, and Early-Career Hiring
design: Occupation, region and firm DiD; joint WFH and AI exposure
verified_finding: AI coefficients attenuate sharply and often lose significance when WFH enters jointly; WFH remains predictive.
caveat: Not proof WFH fully explains every payroll finding; primary abstract supports attenuation, not a universal zero or sign reversal.

authors: Robert W. Fairlie and Jane Wu
title: The Early Impacts of AI on Employment among Recent College Graduates
verification: Primary NBER bibliographic record verified; full text fetch blocked
design: Summer comparisons and relative-group designs, as supplied
verified_finding: Exact summer coefficients and power bounds not independently audited in full text.
caveat: Include as aggregate/recent-graduate counterpoint with verification flag; user/review null and 2–3 pp power claims remain provisional here.

authors: Martha Gimbel and Molly Kinder and Joshua Kendall and Maddie Lee
title: Evaluating the Impact of AI on the Labor Market: Current State of Affairs
data: US CPS occupational composition and AI-use/exposure indicators
verified_finding: Article emphasises aggregate stability rather than widespread labour-market disruption.
caveat: Verified article dated October 1, 2025. Synthetic DiD not found in this article; do not attach a later design to this citation without its own version.

authors: Zanna Iscenko and Fabien Curto Millet
title: Looking for the Ladder: Is AI Impacting Entry-Level Jobs?
verified_finding: Argues monetary tightening and pre-ChatGPT hiring weakness offer alternative explanations.
caveat: Policy essay, not a new causal estimate establishing macro shocks as the sole cause.

title: Labor Market Consequences of Generative AI: Early Evidence from Norway
design: Within-firm composition DiD, occupation synthetic DiD, firm shift-share
verified_finding: No robust young-worker displacement; small negative estimates statistically insignificant.
caveat: Separate paper from Hernæs–Kostøl; shorter outcome horizon; insignificance alone is not equivalence.

authors: Øystein Hernæs and Andreas R. Kostøl
title: Has AI Widened Employment Gaps? Tracking Early-Career Employment by Occupational Exposure in Norway
verification: Primary abstract and pretrend discussion verified
design: Exposure quintiles, cell/firm FE; pretrend sensitivity
verified_finding: Most-exposed employment +0.1% versus +0.3% least-exposed; young complete-quintile comparison is imprecise zero.
caveat: Pretrend tests reject across age groups; selected young software-developer declines are not a whole-quintile effect.
version: June 2026 manuscript in July repository path

authors: Ara Kharazian and Lisa Simon and Ryan Stevens
title: A New Look at AI’s Impact on Jobs
data: Ramp spending linked to Revelio workforce records; 21,559 US firms
design: Adoption event study with eventual-intensity not-yet-treated comparisons
verified_finding: High-intensity adopters expand entry-level headcount about 12%; low-intensity adopters show no significant total employment change.
caveat: Entry-level headcount is not hires; selected firms and adoption intensity may track growth; firm gains do not identify aggregate gains.
